<thought>We need the number of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms (unique proton environments) for the compound in question. The only way to obtain this information is to get its ¹H NMR spectrum, which will list the distinct signals. The tool proton_nmr_spectra returns the spectrum for the target compound (the SMILES is implicitly known from the task context). We'll call it and then count the distinct peaks.</thought>
<action>proton_nmr_spectra</action>
